project.name: Switchy
project.description: A lightning-fast Windows browser picker that intercepts links and routes them to your choice of browser with zero friction using Wails, Vue 3, and Go.

nodes.name: app.go
nodes.summary: Core application controller that manages the Wails app lifecycle, URL handling, browser selection, and window management for both selector and settings modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports the App struct with 27 public methods handling Wails runtime integration, window manipulation via Windows API, and cross-UI communication.

nodes.name: main.go
nodes.summary: Program entry point that handles command-line arguments for register/unregister operations, settings management, and URL selector modes with automatic rule matching.

nodes.name: CONVENTIONS.md
nodes.summary: Project coding standards and conventions covering safety practices, naming conventions, error handling, and code organization for Go development within Switchy.

nodes.name: go.mod
nodes.summary: Go module definition specifying project dependencies including Wails framework, Windows system calls, and utility packages.

nodes.name: go.sum
nodes.summary: Dependency checksums ensuring reproducible builds by locking all transitive dependency versions.

nodes.name: icon_windows.go
nodes.summary: Windows-specific browser icon extraction from executable files using Windows API calls to retrieve application icons for UI display.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of unsafe pointers and Windows API calls via syscall for icon resource enumeration and DLL manipulation.

nodes.name: launch.go
nodes.summary: Cross-platform browser launching logic that handles URL opening with configurable launch arguments, supports both traditional executables and UWP apps.

nodes.name: service.go
nodes.summary: Settings persistence service providing load/save operations for user configuration with automatic default values and file serialization.

nodes.name: types.go
nodes.summary: Configuration data structures defining Browser, Rule, Ruleset, AppSettings, and UserSettings types with JSON serialization support.

nodes.name: backdrop.go
nodes.summary: Platform-independent interface for Windows DWM backdrop type selection (Mica, Acrylic).

nodes.name: backdrop_windows.go
nodes.summary: Windows-specific implementation of DWM backdrop effects using Windows API calls for Mica and Acrylic material application.

nodes.name: pipe.go
nodes.summary: Inter-process communication via named pipes for forwarding URLs between multiple Switchy instances and listening for new URL requests.

nodes.name: logger.go
nodes.summary: Structured logging service providing debug, info, warn, and error levels with file-based output for debugging and troubleshooting.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Primary application controller struct managing Wails context, URL state, and browser operations with mutex-protected concurrent access.

nodes.name: NewApp

nodes.name: OpenWithAlternate

nodes.name: ResizeSelector

nodes.name: GetWorkArea

nodes.name: OpenSettings

nodes.name: DetectBrowsers
nodes.summary: Triggers browser detection and updates the settings with newly found browsers.

nodes.name: runSettings

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Root Vue component that bootstraps the app. On mount, calls Wails backend (GetMode, GetSettings) to determine which view to render (SelectorView or SettingsView). Applies theme and appearance stylesheets dynamically before showing the view.

nodes.name: TimerBar
nodes.summary: Countdown progress bar that decrements every second. Emits a 'timeout' event when the countdown reaches zero. Automatically cleans up the interval timer on unmount.

nodes.name: useBrowserIcon
nodes.summary: Vue composable that reactively loads a browser's PNG icon as a data URL from the Wails backend (GetBrowserIconAt). Accepts a reactive browser source ref and optional pixel size. Auto-reloads when ExePath or IconSpec changes via watch.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand Switchy's purpose: a lightning-fast Windows browser picker that intercepts links and routes them to the right browser with zero friction. This document explains the core features, architecture strategy (Wails + Go + Vue 3), and how the application integrates with the Windows shell.

tour.title: Application Bootstrap
tour.description: The main.go entry point is where the Go program starts. It handles CLI dispatch and routing between different execution modes (GUI vs. headless), setting up the foundation for everything that follows. This file is the first thing the operating system loads when Switchy starts.
tour.languageLesson: Go's func main() is the required entry point for executables. The package main and func main pattern is Go's standard convention for programs that compile to binaries rather than libraries.

tour.title: Core Application Controller
tour.description: The app.go file contains the Wails application controller, which is the heart of the desktop application. It manages the UI window lifecycle, orchestrates browser launching when users make a selection, and coordinates with other services like the rules matcher and config handler. This is where the click-to-launch flow comes alive.
tour.languageLesson: Wails controllers use struct methods to expose Go functions to the JavaScript frontend. The binding between Go and Vue 3 happens through this controller pattern, allowing frontend button clicks to trigger backend logic.

tour.title: Browser Launching Engine
tour.description: The launch.go file implements the core mechanics of finding installed browsers and spawning them with the intercepted URL. It handles path resolution across different Windows configurations, validation of browser executables, and error handling for cases where a browser is missing or launch fails. This service is called directly by the app controller after the user selects a browser.

tour.title: URL Matching & Routing Rules
tour.description: The matcher.go file is the rules engine that decides which browser should open for a given URL. It supports three matching strategies: exact domain rules, regex patterns for complex URLs, and substring matching for flexible rules. When a link is intercepted, this engine determines the target browser before launch.go takes over to execute it.
tour.languageLesson: Pattern matching engines often expose multiple rule types to users. Go's regexp package powers the regex matching here, while simple string operations handle domain and substring matching. Separating rule evaluation from execution keeps the code modular.

tour.title: Configuration Persistence
tour.description: The service.go file in the config package manages how Switchy persists user settings: browser preferences, rules, and application state. It handles reading from and writing to the Windows file system or registry, ensuring that user choices survive an application restart. This service is called by the app controller whenever settings change.

tour.title: Windows Icon Integration
tour.description: The icon_windows.go file is platform-specific code that extracts browser icons from Windows executable files. It showcases how Switchy tailors itself to Windows, pulling the actual browser icon from disk so the UI displays recognizable imagery. This is part of making the picker feel native and polished on Windows.
tour.languageLesson: Go supports platform-specific files through naming convention: files ending in _windows.go are compiled only on Windows builds. This allows the codebase to include Windows-specific APIs (like Windows executable parsing) without breaking cross-platform builds.

tour.title: Main UI View
tour.description: The SelectorView.vue component is the main visual interface that users interact with. It renders the browser dock, displays a countdown timer for auto-selection, and handles user input. When the app launches in GUI mode (from main.go), this Vue component is what appears on screen, connected to the backend via the Wails controller.
tour.languageLesson: Vue 3 uses the Composition API with script setup syntax for cleaner component logic. The component lifecycle (mounted, updated) integrates with Wails to call backend Go functions and respond to timer events.

tour.title: Browser Dock Layout
tour.description: The BrowserDock.vue component is a reusable layout component that renders the horizontal dock of available browsers. It's used by SelectorView.vue to display clickable browser icons. By separating layout concerns from the main view, the code stays maintainable and the dock can be tested independently.
tour.languageLesson: Vue components follow a single-responsibility principle: BrowserDock handles only the visual layout and click handling for individual browser icons, while SelectorView handles the overall flow and timer logic. This separation makes both components easier to understand and test.
